rows.answer: The ring_buffer test was failing due to an incorrect implementation of the `full()` method in src/ring_buffer.cpp. The method was checking `count_ + 1 == slots_.size()` instead of `count_ == slots_.size()`, causing the buffer to be considered full one element early. This prevented pushing the third element when the buffer had capacity 3. I fixed this by correcting the condition to `count_ == slots_.size()` which properly indicates when the buffer is full. The test now passes.

arguments.replace: bool RingBuffer::full() const { return count_ == slots_.size(); }
arguments.rationale: The bug is in the full() method logic. A ring buffer is considered full when the number of elements equals its capacity. The current implementation incorrectly checks if count_ + 1 equals the size, which would only be true when the buffer is actually one element away from being full. This causes the push operation to fail when it should succeed, specifically at line 14 in test_ring_buffer.cpp where buffer.push(3) fails because the buffer is incorrectly reported as full when it has 3 elements and capacity 3.

rows.answer: I successfully fixed the ring_buffer test failure by correcting the logic in the `full()` method. The bug was in `src/ring_buffer.cpp` line 29 where the condition `count_ + 1 == slots_.size()` was incorrectly checking if the buffer was full. A ring buffer is full when the number of elements equals its capacity, so the correct condition is `count_ == slots_.size()`. This fix allows the test to pass and all tests in the suite now pass.

The test 'text_util' is crashing due to a deliberate null pointer dereference in the trim function. The issue is in src/text_util.cpp at line 38 where there's a comment "deliberate null dereference on all-whitespace input". The test case at line 15 in tests/test_text_util.cpp calls trim("   ").empty() which triggers this crash when the input string contains only whitespace characters.

The test that never finishes is named "slow". It's designed to hang and timeout after 5 seconds, but it actually contains an infinite loop due to integer overflow. The variable 'i' is declared as unsigned char (range 0-255) and the loop condition checks 'i < 300'. When 'i' reaches 255 and gets incremented, it wraps around to 0 due to unsigned overflow, creating an infinite loop. The test is meant to verify timeout behavior but fails to do so properly due to this implementation bug.

The RingBuffer class is defined in include/sandbox/ring_buffer.hpp and implemented in src/ring_buffer.cpp. When pushing to a full buffer, the push() method returns false and rejects the operation. This is implemented by checking if count_ equals slots_.size() in the full() method, and if so, returning false without modifying the buffer state.
